messages.subject: regionCounts not extracting data from GRanges file
messages.subject_clean: regionCounts not extracting data from GRanges file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Altuna,

I have a set of promoter regions for which I wanted to summarise methylation data by using methylCounts.

promoters_meth_level<-regionCounts(meth, new_GR, strand.aware = TRUE)

Once I was looking into the output data, I have seen that the regions from "new_GR" are not present in the results...
I have repeated this by looking into one unique promoter, and the output then showed methylation counts for the  specified regions. Do you know what could be the issue? This is a bit worrying!

head(new_GR)
GRanges object with 6 ranges and 0 metadata columns:
      seqnames          ranges strand
         <Rle>       <IRanges>  <Rle>
  [1]        1 1097677-1101807      +
  [2]        1 1101966-1103136      +
  [3]        1 1101966-1103136      +
  [4]        1 1103334-1103488      +
  [5]        1 1104189-1104476      +
  [6]        1 1217160-1217401      +
  -------
  seqinfo: 22 sequences from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

head(promoters_meth_level)
methylBase object with 6 rows
--------------
  chr    start      end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2 coverage3 numCs3 numTs3 coverage4 numCs4 numTs4 coverage5 numCs5
1   1  1097677  1101807      +       164     37    127       217     93    124       210    113     97       243     68    175       189     47
2   1 10743534 10743965      +       117    102     15       106     87     19        88     79      9       101     80     21        89     84
3   1 12251719 12252533      +        52     32     20        54     33     21        48     32     16        64     36     28        55     40
4   1 13911015 13911269      +       143     77     66        71     27     45       158     75     83       180     51    129       148     90

The regions in red are not in the output file, even though I am only showing the first regions, this is the case for other regions too.
Any thoughts why this could be happening? Please advise.

Thanks!
Clara

messages.subject: Error in running calculateDiffMeth
messages.body_plain:
Hi Altuna,

I am trying to remove some chromosomes from my differential methylation analysis which are chrX and chrY.

Used this code:
myobj4 = methRead(location = file.list, sample.id <http://sample.id> = list("A3","A4","A6", "A7", "A8", "A22", "A247", "P018"),
                  assembly = "hg19", dbtype = "tabix", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                  header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t", resolution = "base",
                  treatment = c(1,1,1,1,1,0,0,0), dbdir = "ALS_methyl_call", mincov = 10, )

meth.min_4=unite(myobj4,min.per.group = 3L)

test_methmin4 <- getMembers(meth.min_4)

meth.min_4_removedXY <- test_methmin4[which(test_methmin4$chr != "chrX" & test_methmin4$chr != "chrY"),]

mydiff_5_removedXY = calculateDiffMeth(meth.min_4_removedXY)
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘calculateDiffMeth’ for signature ‘"data.frame"’

Could you please help how can I calculateDiffMeth, again?

Much appreciate it!

Thank you,
Shruti

messages.subject: NA value after tileMethylCounts function
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm using tileMethylCounts function to get methylation regions, and trying to find subgroup within one group (i.e. treatment).

However, I got some NA value in some samples at some regions, for example:

chr.      start    end       sample1         sample2           sample3                 sample4       ...
chr1  10501  11000     97.8891821    93.6908517      NA                         98.0281690
chr1 713001 713500  15.8227848     NA                   32.77027027          25.65055762
chr1 714001 714500  40.9090909     NA                   NA                          NA
...

my data is RRBS on human sample.

If I want to use those regions to cluster, to find subgroup, how should I deal with NA? exclude or assign some value (0/50) to them?

Hope this is clear. Thanks for your time.

Best regards,
Joey
